claim: Upper limits from a pilot search of one SPHEREx pass per field. Not a detection claim; no candidate planet is reported.

tile_rule.text:
Rule (recorded in tiles.json with the parameters and the population's SHA256):
1. Local sky density of the full reference population (2018 positions) around each member,
   top-hat kernel of KERNEL_DEG.
2. Eligible members: |b| >= B_MIN_DEG + the tile's half-diagonal, so the whole tile is
   outside |b| < 15.
3. Keep the densest DENSE_FRACTION of eligible members (density >= that quantile): the
   region holding that share of the |b| > 15 probability mass.
4. Walk those members in a seeded random order (so tiles fall in proportion to density
   inside the region) and accept one as a tile centre if it is at least MIN_SEP_DEG from
   every accepted centre, until N_RANKED tiles. The order is the rank; the search takes the
   first N that pass the SPHEREx coverage pre-flight.

statement: Over 3.6 deg^2 (32 fields of 20 arcmin) of the densest |b| > 15 deg part of the Brown & Batygin (2021) reference population, no moving source brighter than 329 uJy at 1 um (V ~ 18.0) at 30-1000 au in a single SPHEREx pass, at 90% completeness pooled over the fields (50%: 121 uJy, V ~ 19.0), apart from the 18 listed peaks above their field's null maximum. This excludes none of the favoured Planet Nine cases.

peaks.note: Real and mirrored-null searches are statistically alike, so in pure noise about half the fields would have a real peak above their null maximum.

assessment.why: Most likely noise. S/N 7.06 against this field's null maximum 6.80 (a 0.26 margin); of the 27 fields with any peak at S/N >= 7, about half would show a real peak above their own null maximum by chance. Flux 56 +- 8 uJy is below the field's 50% completeness flux (66 uJy). Both halves contribute (5.7 / 4.5), the coadd is a faint compact blob with no star residual, no Gaia source brighter than G 19.3 or CatWISE source brighter than W1 16.2 within 60 arcsec, and no JPL-catalogued body (V < 25) within 60 arcsec. Its best track implies 30-37 au (1.9 arcsec/h). Not followed up in another pass.
Second half only (1.9 / 11.8); dipole in the coadd beside a G 10.5 / W1 9.2 star 22 arcsec away.
First half only (25.2 / 0.0); ring around a masked core; G 8.2 star 33 arcsec away (a Gaia G < 16 star 2.8 px from the peak).
Subtraction dipole in the coadd, 32 arcsec from a W1 7.8 / G 11.3 star.
Masked saturated core with a dipole in the coadd; half-pass S/N lopsided (2.8 / 10.7).

assessment.verdict: artefact: one half of the pass only
assessment.why: First half only (8.1 / 0.8); diffuse coadd 30 arcsec from a G 9.7 / W1 8.6 star.
S/N 7.37 against null maximum 7.31; linear streak-like structure across the coadd; flux 65 uJy, below this field's 50% flux.
S/N 7.35 against null maximum 7.31; coincides (3.4 arcsec) with a G 18.4 / W1 16.3 source; dark streak through the coadd.
Coadd is a large masked saturated star with a ring.

assessment.verdict: artefact: one half of the pass only

All of the S/N from one frame (one frame on the track, share 1.0); second half 0.0.

population.note: Positions at the 2018.4 epoch; local density from a top-hat kernel, so the per-tile mass is a smoothed estimate. Completeness is interpolated at each member's V converted to 1 um for a solar-coloured body; members beyond 1000 au count as not excluded (the capped variant also drops members beyond the field's at-rest motion distance).

planetx_reach.note: SPHEREx D1 AB of each web/data/planetx-limits.json case (lo/nom/hi as there) against the pooled limit; reach capped at 1000 au.
